vsl_script.text:
AI AUTOMATION AUDIT VSL. Target length 60 to 90 seconds. Founder on camera, with a short Command Center screen recording using synthetic data only.

[BEAT 1. HOOK]
You do not need another list of AI tools. You need to know which piece of work is worth removing first. If leads wait, handoffs get missed or the same admin gets repeated every week, bring that workflow to a 15-minute audit.

[BEAT 2. THE PROBLEM]
Most automation projects start with a tool and go hunting for a use. That is why they create another dashboard without giving the owner any time back. We start with the bottleneck: what enters, who touches it, where it waits and what a good result looks like.

[BEAT 3. WHAT HAPPENS]
First, you show us the workflow that creates the most drag. Second, we map the trigger, the systems involved and the decision points that still need a person. Third, we identify the smallest useful automation and the safe next step. If the right answer is not to automate it yet, we will tell you that plainly.

[BEAT 4. WHAT YOU LEAVE WITH]
You leave with a quick-win roadmap: what to automate first, what inputs it needs, where a human approval belongs and what should wait. It is a diagnostic, not a generic pitch deck.

[BEAT 5. CALL TO ACTION]
Answer the short form below and choose a 15-minute time. Bring the messy workflow. We will bring a clear map. If you are not ready to book, the free community is linked below this video.

sections.eyebrow: The expensive part is the waiting
sections.title: The bottleneck is usually between the tools

items.title: Leads wait for a reply
items.body: The enquiry arrived, but the next action still depends on someone seeing it and remembering what to send.

items.title: Handoffs live in people's heads
items.body: The process works when the right person is online, and stalls when they are busy.

items.title: Admin repeats every week
items.body: Copying data, checking status and sending the same update keep taking time because no system owns the whole loop.

items.title: New tools add another inbox
items.body: A point solution moves the work without removing it, so the owner still watches every step.

sections.title: A focused diagnostic, not a software tour
sections.lede: We use the call to make the first automation decision concrete.

items.title: The bottleneck in plain language
items.body: The trigger, the delay, the owner and the outcome are mapped around the way your business works now.

items.title: The smallest useful automation
items.body: A first build that removes a complete piece of work instead of creating another dashboard to manage.

items.title: Human approvals placed on purpose
items.body: The decisions that need judgment stay visible. Repetitive movement and follow-up become candidates for automation.

items.title: A practical next step
items.body: Build it yourself, use a packaged blueprint or scope a Command Center deployment only when the fit is clear.

items.a: Yes. Bring one workflow, not the whole company. The goal is to identify the first useful move and what information a deeper build would need.

items.q: Do I need to prepare anything?
items.a: Know where the workflow starts, which tools it touches and where it usually waits. Screenshots are helpful but not required.

items.q: Will you recommend OASIS either way?
items.a: No. The right next step may be a DIY protocol, a Command Center deployment, a larger fleet audit or no build yet.
You leave with the recommended first move. If an OASIS build makes sense, we can scope it separately. The audit does not switch anything on.
